items.item: A buffer that held every reading is not the same claim as a replay that delivers every reading exactly once, in order, at a rate the platform can absorb.

at.step: Hook: a buffered outage replays wrong on the way back

items.item: The honest prediction isn't a bigger buffer — it's that holding the data was never the hard part; replaying it safely and at a sane pace is.

at.step: Predict: what was missing from the replay?

items.item: A buffer that lives only in memory is a promise that breaks the moment the process restarts, which is exactly when a plant most needs it kept.

at.step: Reveal: the buffer itself is durable and sized from the outage

items.item: A sequence number borrowed from a wire protocol inherits that protocol's own limits; a gateway that needs more room has to build its own key, not stretch someone else's byte.

at.step: Reveal: a wider sequence key makes a duplicate resend idempotent

items.item: Catching up is not just 'go faster' — a replay that ignores the live stream it's running alongside turns a recovery into a second outage for everyone still online.

at.step: Reveal: Little's law sizes the catch-up throttle

items.item: A policy that looks fair because it treats every point the same is exactly how a safety alarm ends up discarded alongside routine noise.

at.step: Reveal: a full buffer drops by priority, never by backpressure

items.item: Trading detail for durability on purpose, before the buffer forces the trade on you by overflowing, is a design decision, not a fallback.

at.step: Reveal: a local rollup extends the outage a fixed buffer survives

items.item: A clock that drifted quietly for the whole outage doesn't announce itself; it just waits for the moment two clocks can finally be compared again.

at.step: Reveal: the gateway's own clock offset is corrected on reconnect

items.item: Every piece of this topic reduces to the same move: the gateway earns the plant's trust one property at a time, and losing any single one quietly breaks what it promised overall.

at.step: Recap

items.item: Plant autonomy isn't something the gateway grants during an outage — it's a property of the control loop that was never the gateway's to take away in the first place.

at.step: Prove it: does the plant keep reading during the outage?

items.item: A gateway that never backpressures its own source isn't being generous — refusing a write from a live PLC is the one failure mode a buffer exists specifically to prevent.
